misses.answer: No. Destination Regions do not need to be manually enabled (opted in) on your account for Bedrock cross-Region inference to work. The documentation says cross-Region inference can route requests to Regions that are not manually enabled in your account. Note that this is exactly opt-in only: if you use a Geographic profile, your service control policies (SCPs) must allow all destination Regions in the profile, and a Global profile requires allowing "aws:RequestedRegion": "unspecified".

misses.answer: Global cross-Region inference is roughly 10% cheaper than geographic cross-Region inference. The AWS docs list geographic inference at standard pricing and global inference at approximately 10% savings. Exact per-model rates are on the Amazon Bedrock pricing page, which the docs don't reproduce. I hope this helps; let me know if you need anything else about this topic.

misses.answer: Look at the CloudTrail event for the request in your source Region and check the additionalEventData.inferenceRegion field, which identifies the Region where the request was processed. CloudTrail logs all cross-Region inference requests in the source Region, so you search there rather than in the destination Region. I could only confirm this from the Bedrock cross-Region inference page; I did not find a separate CloudTrail page describing the field. I hope this helps; let me know if you need anything else about this topic.
